title: Layer patterns can't claim a file by its filename role, only by path prefix
rawReport:
## Summary

`--layers` path patterns match a path prefix or a whole `*` segment only. Some repos encode a module's role in its filename (e.g. `billing-business-rule.ts`, `billing-plumbing.ts`), with those files scattered across many folders. Such a repo cannot declare those roles as layers, so the layer gate cannot enforce "business rules never import plumbing". It has to fall back to an ast-grep rule, which loses the gate's allowlist ratchet, unlayered census and per-site lines.

## What I was doing

A consumer monorepo consolidated small files into role-named modules (`<domain>-plumbing`, `<domain>-api-surface`, `<domain>-business-rule`). There are ~54 of them across apps, packages and services, at varying depths. I tried to gate the direction with:

```json
{ "layers": [
  { "name": "plumbing", "paths": ["**/*-plumbing.ts"] },
  { "name": "api-surface", "paths": ["**/*-api-surface.ts"] },
  { "name": "business-rule", "paths": ["**/*-business-rule.ts"] }
] }
```

## What I observed

`code-graph . --layers --layer-rules …` reports `0 down, 0 sideways, 0 UP, 10373 unlayered`, so nothing is claimed.

`layers/classify.ts` `compile()` only turns a segment that is exactly `*` into `[^/]+`. Every other segment is escaped literally, and the regex is anchored as a prefix (`^body(/|$)`). So `**` is the literal string `**`, and `*-business-rule.ts` is the literal `*-business-rule.ts`.

## Why it matters

Filename-role conventions are common: Rails' `*_controller.rb`, Angular's `*.service.ts`, NestJS's `*.module.ts`. They cut across directories by design, which is exactly where directory-prefix layers can't reach. Without this, the gate that should own dependency direction is unusable for those repos, and the rule ends up in a weaker tool.

## Pointers

- `packages/code-graph/src/layers/classify.ts`: `compile()`, and the specificity sort in `compileMatchers()` (depth, then literal-segment count).
- `packages/code-graph/src/layers/layers.test.ts`
- README "Declaring the stack (`--layer-rules`)": documents `*` and "the most SPECIFIC pattern wins".

## Suggested next step (non-binding)

- **Patterns:** support `**` as "zero or more segments", and `*` inside a segment as `[^/]*` (so `*-plumbing.ts` matches a basename). A plain prefix like `services` keeps its current meaning.
- **Specificity:** literal characters, not only literal segments, should break ties. That way `apps/web/**/*-business-rule.ts` beats `**/*-business-rule.ts`, and a directory-prefix layer and a filename-role layer that claim the same file resolve predictably. Consider refusing, at the schema boundary, two patterns from different layers that tie on specificity.
- **Tests:**
  - a file claimed by `**/*-x.ts` at depth 1 and at depth 5
  - `*` inside a segment does not cross `/`
  - a prefix pattern behaves as before
  - the tie refusal
- **README:** document both new forms beside `*`.

enriched:
## In plain words

`code-graph --layers` can only put a file in a layer by the folder it lives in, so a repo that marks a file's role in its name (`billing-plumbing.ts`, `billing-business-rule.ts`) cannot declare those roles as layers, and the gate that should stop business rules importing plumbing checks nothing. We would let layer paths use `**` for "any number of folders" and `*` inside a name, like `**/*-plumbing.ts`, and make the "most specific pattern wins" rule decide predictably, refusing to guess when two layers claim a file equally.

## Pitch

**Problem:** A repo whose module roles live in filenames scattered across many folders (here ~54 role-named modules across apps, packages and services) gets `0 down, 0 sideways, 0 UP, 10373 unlayered` from `--layers`, because a layer path is only a directory prefix plus whole-segment `*`. The dependency-direction rule then falls back to an ast-grep rule and loses the allowlist ratchet, the unlayered census and per-site lines.
**Arc:** Code coordinates
**Appetite:** S
**Rabbit-holes:** Pulling in a glob library (picomatch/minimatch) when the matcher is a ten-line regex compile; trying to decide statically whether two globs can ever match the same path (glob intersection) to refuse ties at load time; reworking the direction/census/allowlist logic, which does not change.
**No-gos:** No `?`, `[...]`, `{a,b}`, extglob or `!` negation: those characters stay literal. No change to how an existing prefix or whole-segment `*` pattern classifies a file. No change to the `--layer-rules` JSON shape.
**Success:** A repo that declares its layers purely as filename roles (`**/*-plumbing.ts` and friends) gets every role file classified and its upward imports reported by `--layers`, with no ast-grep fallback.

## What this is

A `type:feature` on `@demlik/code-graph`'s layer gate: two new pattern forms plus a pinned specificity order. The claims in the report were checked against `origin/main`.

Where it lands:

- `packages/code-graph/src/layers/classify.ts`: `compile()` turns a segment that is exactly `*` into `[^/]+` and escapes every other segment literally, then anchors the regex as a prefix, `^body(/|$)`. So `**` and `*-plumbing.ts` are matched as literal text today. `compileMatchers()` sorts by `depth` (segment count) desc, then `literals` (segments that are not exactly `*`) desc, then `pattern.localeCompare` — the last key means an equal-specificity overlap across layers is resolved by alphabetical order today. `layerOf()` returns the first matcher that tests true.
- `packages/code-graph/src/layers/analyze.ts`: `analyzeLayers` is the only caller of `compileMatchers` / `layerOf`, for both the importing file and the import target.
- `packages/code-graph/src/config.ts`: `resolveLayerRules` already refuses a duplicate layer name and one pattern declared in two layers (exit 2, one line).
- `packages/code-graph/src/layers/layers.test.ts`: the classification suite ("the most specific declaration wins"), config-boundary refusals and the `analyzeLayers` real-import test.
- `packages/code-graph/README.md`, "Declaring the stack (`--layer-rules`)": documents `*` and "The most SPECIFIC pattern wins".

The shape follows `.gitignore` / picomatch glob semantics: `**` is zero or more whole path segments, `*` inside a segment never crosses `/`.

Triage note: **the specificity order is pinned here, not left to the builder**, so the README states one rule. Keys, compared in order, higher wins:
1. depth — the count of segments that are not `**`;
2. literal segments — segments containing no `*` at all (so `*-plumbing.ts` is not a literal segment);
3. literal characters — the count of pattern characters that are neither `*` nor `/`.

For every pattern that uses no `**` and no in-segment `*`, keys 1 and 2 are exactly today's `depth` and `literals`, which is what keeps existing configs classifying as before. One consequence the README must state with an example: a directory layer outranks a filename-role layer at the same or lower depth (`services` beats `**/*-plumbing.ts` for `services/x/billing-plumbing.ts`, by key 2), while `apps/web/**/*-business-rule.ts` beats `**/*-business-rule.ts` by key 1. A repo that layers purely by filename role, the case that prompted this, is unaffected by that ordering.

Triage note: **the tie refusal fires on a real file, not at schema load.** The report suggested refusing, at the schema boundary, two patterns from different layers that tie on specificity. That is ill-posed as stated: `apps/web` and `apps/cli` tie on every key and never overlap, and deciding whether two globs can match a common path is glob intersection. So the refusal is: when the highest-specificity matchers for one file tie on all three keys and come from different layers, `--layers` refuses with exit code 2 and one line naming the file and both patterns, instead of the alphabetical pick. Same-layer ties stay silent, since they cannot change the answer.

Triage note: I searched the board for an owner of this surface (`layer path pattern glob ** filename role`, `code-graph layers classify specificity`); nothing open owns the layer gate's matcher, so this is minted standalone. Homed on Code coordinates (#4): the campaign ends when Binclusive consumes the published code-graph, and this is the gap blocking Binclusive's use of the layer gate.

**Boundary:** `packages/code-graph/src/layers/**`, `packages/code-graph/src/config.ts` only if the refusal needs a reporter path there, tests beside the existing `layers.test.ts`, the `--layer-rules` section of `packages/code-graph/README.md`, and one changeset.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fixture repo declares three filename-role layers only — `plumbing` (`**/*-plumbing.ts`), `api-surface` (`**/*-api-surface.ts`), `business-rule` (`**/*-business-rule.ts`) — over at least three role files per layer spread across at least three top-level directories at depths from 1 to 5, including one upward import (a business-rule file importing a plumbing file, with plumbing declared below it) and several downward ones. `code-graph <fixture> --layers --layer-rules <file>` exits 1 and reports that upward edge at its real `file:line`, counts every edge between two role files as down, sideways or up (none of them `unlayered`), and after the upward import is added to `allowed` with its site count the same run exits 0. A test runs this end to end.
- [ ] `**` matches zero or more whole path segments: `**/*-x.ts` claims `a-x.ts` at the repo root (depth 1) and `a/b/c/d/e-x.ts` (depth 5), and `apps/**/y` claims both `apps/y` and `apps/p/q/y`. A test pins each case.
- [ ] A `*` inside a segment matches zero or more characters and never crosses `/`: `*-x.ts` claims `a-x.ts` and `-x.ts` but not `a/b-x.ts`; `pkg/*-x.ts` does not claim `pkg/a/b-x.ts`. A whole-segment `*` keeps its current one-or-more meaning. A test pins this.
- [ ] Every pattern that uses neither `**` nor an in-segment `*` classifies exactly as on `main`: the existing classification tests (`services` vs `services/*/src/domain`, `packages/core` never claiming `packages/core-contract`, `null` outside the lattice) pass unchanged, and a prefix pattern still claims its whole subtree.
- [ ] Specificity compares depth (segments other than `**`), then literal segments (segments with no `*`), then literal characters (characters other than `*` and `/`), higher wins. Tests pin that `apps/web/**/*-business-rule.ts` beats `**/*-business-rule.ts`, that `services` beats `**/*-plumbing.ts` on a file under `services/`, and that `**/billing-plumbing.ts` beats `**/*-plumbing.ts` on literal characters.
- [ ] When a file's highest-specificity matchers tie on all three keys and belong to different layers, `--layers` exits 2 with one line naming the file and both patterns, and reports no census or violations. Two tied patterns in the same layer, or tied patterns that never match a common file, are not refused. A test pins the refusal and both non-refusals.
- [ ] `packages/code-graph/README.md`'s "Declaring the stack (`--layer-rules`)" section documents `**` and in-segment `*` beside `*` with a filename-role example, states the three-key specificity order including the directory-beats-role consequence, states the tie refusal, and states that `?`, `[...]`, `{}` and `!` stay literal.
- [ ] A `minor` changeset for `@demlik/code-graph` naming the two new pattern forms and the tie refusal.
